scope.head: 32b80d5f
scope.activity: read-only exploration; only this evidence artifact written

verdict: Native owner-private Sites is supported and uses ChatGPT authentication. Shared-password-only access is not a native Sites access mode. The inspected contract does not certify Worker-first gating of a separate Nextra static asset bundle. Do not label private ChatGPT login as a shared password.
recommendation: Reuse Nextra static export with native private Sites if ChatGPT identity meets the user's intent. If a shared password is mandatory, resolve that requirement explicitly before publishing or promising it; do not replace it silently. A Worker plus private R2 objects is a capability-supported additional-password architecture, but requires new server/upload implementation and production verification, and preserves ChatGPT sign-in when the Site remains private.

facts.fact: Sites owns hosted authentication; private Sites require authenticated access and visitors sign in. Preserve native authentication instead of scaffolding separate OAuth/session stack.
Allowed request access_mode values are public, workspace_all, custom; allowlists and viewers are supported. There is no shared-password field. No tool invoked.
static only accepts directory and not_found_handling; Worker entrypoint is dist/server/index.js, static mode uses index.html; built static config is forbidden for Worker builds.
Worker mode copies the whole dist tree. This proves archive inclusion, not dispatch order, public routing, or an ASSETS binding.
ESM starter is for microsites, copies only worker/index.js and hosting.json, and forbids standalone assets.
Sites plugin copies hosting manifest and migrations; no run_worker_first or asset routing contract appears in this integration.
Sites provisions R2 bindings declared in hosting.json; R2 is accessed server-side through Workers env.
Private service access and runtime secrets are supported. Secrets must remain out of source, client bundles and hosting manifest.
Official Nextra export uses output: export, images.unoptimized and Pagefind output under out/_pagefind.
R2 buckets are private by default; direct public exposure is opt-in. Sites R2 configuration has not been registered or inspected in production.

boundaries.supported_native_path: Nextra static export -> Sites static package -> native private audience -> ChatGPT login.
boundaries.unproven_path: Nextra out copied alongside Worker -> assume all asset reads pass custom password. No supported Sites setting guaranteeing this was found in the inspected manifests, starter and packager.
boundaries.capability_supported_alternative: Keep Site private, omit static deployment, package server-only Worker and R2 binding. Store all HTML/_next/_pagefind objects in private R2; authorize password server-side before every bucket read. This adds a password after native ChatGPT login, with no standalone public assets. Its object upload and versioning path still needs implementation and verification.
boundaries.password_only: Would require permitting unauthenticated traffic to the Worker, which changes native private access and cannot be done under the instruction to preserve platform identity.

uncertainty: No Site was created, registered, deployed or probed.
Sites backend implementation and generated deployment routing are not available from this local plugin.
No claim of universal impossibility: only native shared-password absence and missing supported Worker-first static-bundle guarantee.
Private R2 is a compositional architecture, not a validated deployment result; no password or secret was created.
